headline: Comparative genomics ties regulatory evolution to lineage-specific innovation
label: Comparative Regulatory Genomics Evolution
summary: Cross-species regulatory maps now resolve conserved non-coding elements, lncRNA orthologs, and gene regulatory networks at scale.
synthesis: The dominant thread is cross-species analysis of regulatory architecture, tracing how non-coding and epigenetic control elements diverge and persist. The axolotl preprint maps regeneration-associated motif grammar onto mammalian loci, with AlphaGenome predicting bivalent dormant chromatin states. Coral work integrates RNA-seq, small RNA-seq and WGBS to map miRNA and lncRNA control of epigenetic genes. CNEwrap and EvoAcc scale detection of conserved non-coding elements and accelerated evolution genome-wide. A lncRNA orthology workflow spans 13 vertebrates with human as reference, and CroCoNet compares single-cell gene regulatory networks across species. The sea pen genome ties lineage-specific luciferin-binding protein expansion to bioluminescence evolution. New is the combination of sequence conservation, chromatin state prediction and network comparison to connect regulatory change with lineage-specific traits.
